methods.name: Covariate balancing propensity score: exact and over-identified, ATE and ATT; logit baseline
methods.reference: CBPS::CBPS(method = 'exact' | 'over', ATT = 0 | 1, standardize = TRUE, twostep = TRUE), CBPS 0.24, and a tight refit of CBPS.2Treat (validation/r/cases/causal_cbps.R); stats::glm(binomial)
quantities: coefficients (exact, over x ATE, ATT; logit)
SE (delta method from the whitened sandwich; glm SE for logit)
package values as a cross-check (exact ATE/ATT, over ATE)
methods.tolerance: n = 400: exact and logit at validation/README.md (coefficients, scores, weights 1e-8; SE and deviance 1e-6 relative); over (GMM) Tol::iterative(1e-6); alpha Tol::iterative(1e-6) and J Tol::iterative(5e-6): CBPS's start objective carries about 1e-12 relative rounding noise, so alpha agrees to about 1e-7; package cross-check Tol::iterative: over ATE 1e-4, exact ATE/ATT 1e-3 (J 2e-3), deviance 1e-6, because CBPS() stops its optimisers at optimize tol eps^0.25 and BFGS reltol 1e-8

deviations.quantity: over-identified ATT (method = 'over', ATT = 1): coefficients, SE, J, scores, weights, deviance
deviations.note: CBPS 0.24's gmm.gradient writes the ATT balance block as 1/n.t * t(X * dw) %*% X, n/n_t times the derivative of its own moment (1/n) X'w, so BFGS stops where its objective's gradient is (3.6e-4, 2.4e-4, -4.2e-5, -3.8e-5); the minimiser has J 0.0017281 against CBPS's 0.0024947. p2a minimises CBPS's objective and is pinned to CBPS.2Treat with that line corrected (over_att_tight_*); CBPS's own over_att_* values are recorded, not compared

CBPS.fit maps CBPS.2Treat's whitened-scale sandwich back with Dx.inv ginv(X'X) X' U V ginv(D) ..., which is not the Jacobian of its coefficient map and not scale-equivariant (x3 * 10 leaves CBPS's x3 SE at 0.109412; bootstrap SE 0.219845, delta method 0.218720). p2a reports T V_u T' / n, T = M V D^-1; CBPS's transform is recorded as *_se_reported, not pinned

deviations.quantity: start scale alpha (and through W the over-identified estimates, about 1e-7)
deviations.note: CBPS takes alpha = optimize(f, c(0.8, 1.1)) with tol eps^0.25; the computed f has about 1e-12 relative rounding noise, so optimize places alpha only to about 1e-7. The reference refines alpha by bisection on f'(alpha); p2a takes Brent's minimiser at tol 1e-12, within about 1e-7
refused (R9, R3); CBPS returns a minimum-norm split for collinear covariates and treats a numeric two-valued treatment as continuous
